acceptance.output_evidence: WHAT AN IN-MEMORY HANDLER CANNOT SHOW, enumerated BY SUBTRACTION from the real request path (browser -> CloudFront -> Lambda@Edge -> API Gateway -> authorizer -> integration -> Lambda container -> handler) rather than by recall, so a stage cannot be dropped without the list disagreeing with the path: (1) CLOUDFRONT -- 28 behaviors on dist EVTSA9VEHNZVH; whether any caches a scoped response at the edge, where NO Lambda runs on a hit. (2) THE EDGE VALIDATOR -- in the battery the nine headers are a dict a test wrote; IB-sb-3 must show the headers arriving at the origin are the INJECTED ones and that a browser-supplied X-User-* really is overwritten in flight. (3) THE API GATEWAY AUTHORIZER -- naqxlm = opal-portal-authorizer, authorization_type CUSTOM, REQUEST type, RS256 via Secrets Manager (api-gateway.tf:7-10,19,28), and CRITICALLY its RESULT CACHE: an authorizer result cache returns a PRIOR allow for the TTL's duration, so a revocation inside that window is invisible to everything downstream -- and the TTL is NOT DECLARED IN THAT TERRAFORM ROOT (the file sets authorizer_id on 13 routes and never the authorizer's own caching), so it must be read from the LIVE authorizer and cannot be inferred from the repo. (4) API GATEWAY / stage RESPONSE caching, which can return a body before the integration is invoked. (5) THE LAMBDA EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT -- a module-level cache surviving across invocations in a warm container, which is exactly what arm (b) simulates in memory and cannot exercise for real. (6) IAM ON THE READ PATH -- whether the role can even fetch the directory the wrapper authorizes against; a permission failure there produces an empty read and must not become an empty SERVED set. (7) CONCURRENCY -- a revocation landing BETWEEN the authorize and the serve of one in-flight request, and two containers disagreeing for the length of a TTL. THE HONEST SUMMARY: the battery proves the LIBRARY re-checks; it proves NOTHING about whether every serving path in the deployed system goes through the library. || CAN THE WRAPPER BE BYPASSED? YES. Nothing in Python can stop a route table pointing at an unwrapped function, and saying otherwise would be the comfortable answer rather than the true one. The wrapper therefore MARKS what it wraps (__irpt_guarded__) and ships unguarded_routes(), a census over the ROUTE TABLE -- what is REACHABLE -- rather than over a module's functions, because an unreferenced unguarded function is not a hole and an unguarded function WIRED TO A ROUTE is. Exercised in the battery: clean table {"guarded": 1, "routes": 1, "unguarded": [], "verdict": "OK: every route is guarded"}; one unwrapped route {"guarded": 1, "routes": 2, "unguarded": ["GET /leak"], "verdict": "BLOCKED: 1 of 2 route(s) reach an unguarded handler"}. FOUR DECLARED LIMITS so no reader over-reads it: (i) it runs where the route table is IMPORTABLE -- a test or build-time check, not a runtime guarantee; nothing refuses to start a Lambda whose handler is unwrapped; (ii) it cannot see a route that reaches a handler without passing through the table it is handed -- a console-wired API Gateway route, or a Terraform-declared route whose Python target this census never imports; A ROUTE TABLE CENSUS IS ONLY AS WIDE AS THE TABLE HANDED TO IT; (iii) it cannot see a wrapped handler whose caller reaches the inner function directly (__irpt_unwrapped__ is kept for testing); (iv) THE STRONGEST VERSION IS NOT THIS CENSUS BUT IB-sb-3's DEPLOYED-ROUTE REPLAY -- for every route that exists in Terraform, send a negative request and require a refusal; that reads the WORLD rather than the code and is the only arm a handler that merely looks wrapped cannot satisfy.

mutant.description: Six mutations, at least one per arm, each aimed at an assertion that would otherwise be a constant: (a) the SAME request with NO swap, which must SERVE -- otherwise six refusals prove only that the wrapper refuses everything -- and the served response run through the SAME byte census that the refusals are graded by; (b) the revoked request replayed after RESTORING the grant, which must hit the same never-evicted cache entry -- otherwise the refusal could be a cold cache; (c) a job still covered at consumption, which must be DELIVERED; (d) well-shaped key components (an ISO date, an enum token), which must be ADMITTED; (e) the firm-authorized viewer pointed at another firm's id and another firm's artifact, which must be REFUSED; plus a MATCHED account through the gap-reason helper, which must produce no gap row.
mutant.expected: (a) ok=True, and the byte census goes NON-ZERO on the served response; (b) cache_hit=True; (c) ok=True; (d) ok=True; (e) both refused.
mutant.observed: (a) 'BASELINE (must SERVE, else six refusals prove only that nothing works): ok=True cache_hit=False accounts=3' and 'POSITIVE CONTROL on the byte census: the SERVED response trips it at 6 of 16 token(s)'; (b) 'OUTCOME 3 -- grant RESTORED, same request: ok=True cache_hit=True'; (c) 'CONTROL: a job still covered at consumption -> ok=True reauthorized_at_consumption=True'; (d) 'NEGATIVE CONTROL: well-shaped components (an ISO date and an enum token) are ADMITTED: ok=True'; (e) '2 of 2 cross-firm attempts by the firm-authorized viewer refused'. AND THE MUTATION THAT ACTUALLY FIRED: arm (d) FAILED on its first run, printing 'the value appears in the refusal: True' for 4 of 4 name-shaped components -- the KEY_REFUSED refusal was echoing the refused client name and e-mail address back to the caller because _keys names the value in its exception text and the wrapper passed str(exc) through. Fixed at the wrapper's boundary (the reason names the offending PARAMETER NAMES, found by re-building the key one parameter at a time through the PUBLIC cache_key API, never by parsing the message); the same four now print False. Filed as row IRPT_BCKEND-W2-S10.
